title: audit: a summary (roll-up) recompute after a child write stamps the child's writer as updated_by on the master record
body:
repo:hotcrm#1 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAnPkgK6CWrJa6t7Fk5

**Measured on 18.5.0** (hotcrm#2487, the Order to Cash write opt-in, CTR-0001).
- A finance user (Accounts Receivable position) inserts an invoice and a payment under contract CTR-0001.
- The contract's and the account's summary fields (invoiced, received, receivable) recompute, as they should.
- Both master records then read **"Updated by Fin AR"** with a fresh `updated_at`, though finance edits neither record and holds no edit on either.
- A sales rep's plan-step write does the same to the contract.

**Why it matters:** `updated_by` / `updated_at` are the audit trail a person reads on the record page. A system-derived recompute shows up as an edit by whoever touched a child. That misleads an auditor, and it can trip "last modified by" list views, flows on `updated_by`, or field history.

**Asked:** a summary recompute (and any derivation-only write the engine makes on a master) leaves `updated_by` untouched, or stamps it as the system. Whether it also leaves `updated_at` alone is part of the design: a figure did change. It writes no field-history row attributed to the child's writer. A test: insert a child as user B under a master owned and last edited by user A, then the master's `updated_by` is still A (or the system), never B.

**Consumer:** hotcrm Order to Cash (contracts, accounts) and PSA (project cost roll-ups) both hit it. No hotcrm workaround planned.
